scope: Public feature-frame restoration timings and a read-only diagnostics entry; no Cython backend yet

shared_components.dataprep/replay_inputs.py: Separate frame/observation file reads and total decode; public InputSession performance collector
shared_components.datahub/features/prepared_frames.py: Arrow materialization, reference checks and frame/snapshot construction
shared_components.datahub/features/restoration.py: Dataset-independent decimal and market-observation batches; no strategy identifiers
shared_components.dataprep/feature_diagnostics.py: Local declared custom-feature provider and the same public decoder, no strategy/engine/native SDK required

collection: Batch clocks per frame, never per observation; phase durations accumulated locally and each published once. Price and object timing separates the former combined comprehension, using a small price list per frame.

compatibility.old_v1_diagnostic: Supported for unchanged v1 file schema; artifact size/schema/rows and current feature source content/schema/record count verified; full optionally verifies read-file SHA256
compatibility.current_implementation_matches_artifact: Explicitly reported; false expected for existing v1 after timing-code changes
compatibility.formal_backtest: Existing exact source/native context comparison remains unchanged and rejects stale implementation identity
compatibility.formal_new_version: New replay-input version required for formal backtest under changed sources; parent prepared snapshot retained; no regeneration needed to run diagnostics

local_tests.environment: Python 3.12; local validation pandas 3.0.6 / PyArrow 25.0.1 / NumPy 2.5.3

checks: Measured/unmeasured restore equals declared custom scalar-feature outcomes without Bar projection
Exact Decimal exponent, visible revision, decision clocks and READY/SKIPPED outcomes preserved
Old implementation identity works only in read-only diagnostic; ordinary ReplayInputs expected-context mismatch still rejected
Repeat diagnostics do not read/replay native market inputs and leave every artifact byte unchanged
Feature schema/content changes and full-check frame corruption rejected
Standalone CLI works without compiled SDK and protects artifact and feature inputs from report writes

future_cython_boundary.target: Shared bulk numeric/observation restoration or typed reference-clock validation after XY measurements identify the dominant phase
future_cython_boundary.contract: Keep a Python path and compare Decimal values/representations, source/availability clocks, revisions and skipped outcomes
future_cython_boundary.limits: Feather I/O and Arrow native-library work are not accelerated by merely compiling Python; Python object allocation/GIL must be measured separately

limits: No native or full-interval performance claim for these changes
Diagnostic still uses existing v1 single-EXACT-feature frame format
Repeated runs reuse OS caches; feature-source setup measured separately from frame restoration
Timing overhead and separated batches can slightly change wall time relative to original combined loop

interpretation: I/O is about 0.028 seconds; field materialization and observation-object construction dominate
Five columns per observation imply 7441870 field values materialized by the observation to_pydict step
Decimal conversion is only 0.37 seconds, not the primary bottleneck; reference checks about 0.08 seconds
Feature source setup is outside the measured frame-restore interval
Single diagnostic run, no strategy or matching engine; not a new full-backtest speed or financial-equivalence claim
proposed_shared_cython_design: Consume Arrow/NumPy column buffers and compact metadata/dictionary codes instead of materializing every observation into Python column lists first
Reuse dictionary-decoded contract/source strings while preserving exact values and mappings
Fuse column access and batch market-observation assembly in a shared Cython boundary; retain the Python path and public object/clock/Decimal contracts
Keep dataset/strategy signal logic out of the accelerator; compiling a caller that still invokes the original to_pydict would retain its cost
Prototype and measure before claiming speedup; Python object allocation remains a cost even with Cython
